name: Enforcer independence
asked: Who funds and staffs the inspector (fees, appropriations, industry assessments), and how it can be overruled.
status_note: status left null on purpose; Lindsay scores

cross_cutting.text: Feb 2025 EO 'Ensuring Accountability for All Agencies' sends independent agencies' significant rules to White House OIRA review. Trump v. Slaughter (June 29, 2026, 6-3) struck the FTC's for-cause removal protection and overturned Humphrey's Executor; Trump v. Cook (5-4, same day) kept Fed Governor Cook in place on narrow procedural grounds. Applies to nuclear, grid and banking rows below.

sources.label: Ballotpedia on Trump v. Slaughter / Cook

cross_cutting.note: Opinion text itself not fetched; secondary sources only.

labs.funding: Federal CLIA is user-fee funded by statute: lab certificate fees plus inspection fees must cover all program costs, surveys included. Accredited labs pay CAP's own accreditation fees.
labs.staffing: CLIA surveys are usually done by state health department staff. CAP inspections are done by volunteer peer teams of practicing lab professionals (CAP cites about 7,750).
labs.overrule: CMS validates accreditors and can withdraw deemed status (42 CFR 488.9, already in R31). CMS sits inside HHS, an executive department: no removal protection to lose.

sources.label: CMS CLIA brochure (fees cover all costs)

labs.note: CA Laboratory Field Services funding source not checked. 'Usually state staff' is from a secondary summary (pathologyoutlines), not fetched from CMS.

nuclear.funding: NEIMA requires NRC to recover about 100% of its budget from licensee fees (10 CFR 170 service fees, 10 CFR 171 annual fees), minus excluded activities. FY2026: about $819.4M billed as fees.
nuclear.staffing: Federal NRC staff, including resident inspectors at plants (R02).
nuclear.overrule: Under the Feb 2025 EO, NRC draft rules go to OIRA; if NRC and OIRA disagree the President decides (per NRC to E&E News). EO 14300 (May 2025) ordered a wholesale rule revision with NRC's DOGE team. The President removed Commissioner Hanson June 14, 2025; he did not challenge it. Slaughter likely reaches NRC's for-cause protection (not yet litigated for NRC).

sources.label: NRC FY2026 final fee rule, 91 FR 36470
E&E News, How the NRC lost its independence

nuclear.note: R31 nuclear (NRC Inspector General) is still 'Not checked'; this row doesn't fill it.

aviation.funding: The Airport and Airway Trust Fund, built from aviation excise taxes on tickets, cargo and fuel, is FAA's primary funding source, including safety inspections; general fund money adds to it.
aviation.staffing: Mixed. FAA inspectors, plus Organization Designation Authorization: a unit of Boeing employees (over 1,000) performs delegated FAA inspections and approvals. Renewed for 3 years from June 1, 2025. FAA fined Boeing in 2020 for managers pressuring ODA staff.
aviation.overrule: NTSB can amend or reverse FAA certificate actions (already in R31). FAA sits inside DOT, an executive department. FAA Administrator removal terms not fetched.

sources.label: FAA statement on Boeing ODA renewal
FAA 2020 civil penalty, undue pressure on designees

aviation.note: Trust fund vs general fund share for FY2026 not pulled.

banking.funding: No appropriations. OCC: about 94% from semiannual assessments on the banks it supervises (12 U.S.C. 481-482); the Comptroller alone decides how funds are spent (12 U.S.C. 16). FDIC: deposit insurance assessments. Fed: its own earnings, budget set internally.
banking.staffing: Federal examiners. Historically, OCC examiners were paid directly by banks to shield them from appropriations pressure.
banking.overrule: Fed governors: for-cause removal held for now (Trump v. Cook, 5-4, narrow; could return). OCC and FDIC leadership: Slaughter's reasoning likely applies; not separately checked. Material-loss IG reviews already in R31.

sources.label: OCC FY2027 Budget in Brief (94% assessments)
Atlanta Fed, Congressional control over banking agencies' budgets
Bloomberg Law on Trump v. Cook

banking.note: The Atlanta Fed piece is from 2017; funding model unchanged per OCC 2027 documents.

pharma.funding: Split. FY2026 request: $3.6B user fees vs $3.2B appropriations. PDUFA fees covered 78% of the drug review program in 2024 (7% in 1993). Review-time goals are negotiated with manufacturers and reauthorized by Congress every 5 years; PDUFA expires Sept 30, 2027.
pharma.staffing: Federal FDA staff; FDA's Office of Inspections and Investigations is its sole field operations office.
pharma.overrule: FDA sits inside HHS, an executive department; the commissioner serves at will. Fee collection is conditioned on Congress keeping FDA's own appropriations at a floor.

sources.label: FDA performance budget (fees negotiated with manufacturers)
CRS R44576 FDA budget fact sheet

pharma.note: Whether inspection staff specifically are fee-funded or appropriation-funded not separated out.

chemical.funding: In California, local CUPAs run the accident-prevention program (CalARP) on fees charged to the regulated businesses, plus a state surcharge per business ($370/yr CalARP as of Oct 2023).
chemical.staffing: Local CUPA staff (county or fire agencies); federal EPA and OSHA staff.
chemical.overrule: OSHA citations (including process safety) can be contested before OSHRC, a separate appropriated adjudicator ($14.2M) independent of OSHA and the Labor Department. EPA retains oversight of delegated programs (R31).

sources.label: CalEPA single-fee statement (CUPAs funded by business fees)

chemical.note: Federal EPA RMP and OSHA PSM budgets not fetched; no user fee found for either in this pass.

grid.funding: NERC and the six Regional Entities are funded by assessments on load-serving entities (16 U.S.C. 824o(c)(2)(B)); FERC approves the budgets. FERC recovers 100% of its own appropriation from annual charges and filing fees on the industry it regulates.
grid.staffing: NERC and Regional Entity staff (private nonprofits; e.g., WECC is a 501(c)(4)). Regional boards include industry-sector representatives (e.g., ReliabilityFirst's six industry sectors).
grid.overrule: FERC approves or remands standards and penalties (R31). FERC commissioners have the same for-cause wording the Court struck for the FTC; law firms read Slaughter as making them very likely removable at will.

sources.label: FERC order on NERC budget citing 824o(c)(2)(B)
Texas RE 2026 budget (LSE assessments)
sources.url: https://nerc.com/gov/bot/FINANCE/RegionalEntityBPandB/Texas RE Draft 2026 Business Plan and Budget.pdf

sources.label: Vinson & Elkins on Slaughter and FERC

grid.note: Who sits on NERC's own board not checked.

supply.funding: CA Board of Pharmacy (which licenses and inspects wholesalers) is entirely self-funded, mainly from license fees; no state general fund money.
supply.staffing: Board inspectors are registered pharmacists. 7 of the 13 board members are licensed pharmacists; the board appoints its own executive officer.
supply.overrule: Boards controlled by active market participants lose antitrust immunity unless actively supervised by the state (NC Dental v. FTC, 2015). Federal FDA wholesaler standard still not final (R31).

sources.label: CA Board of Pharmacy, About the Board

supply.note: DEA (controlled substances) not covered; the map's supply column is DSCSA/wholesalers.

ai.text: No inspector exists to fund or staff (R02 AI: voluntary only). CAISI testing is by invitation. Nothing to score on funding; overrule question doesn't arise.
